To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) We developed and validated a robust and facile assay to measure LRRK2 pathway activity by assessing the phosphorylation of Rab 10 in human neutrophil cells; (2) We used the newly developed MJFF-pRAB10 monoclonal to quantify Rab10 phosphorylation; (3) We showed that the LRRK2 G2019S mutation is associated with increased Rab10 phosphorylation, which may be a useful biomarker for Parkinson9s disease; (
we developed a facile and robust method for measuring LRRK kinase pathway activity in human peripheral blood cells and that this method could be applied in future LRR2 inhibitor trials.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and validation of a novel LRRK2 pathway activity assay that can be used to assess the activity of LRRK kinase inhibitors in the clinic.
the development of a facile, robust and clinically applicable method to interrogate LRRK2 pathway activity in human blood cells.
the development of a robust, reliable and clinically relevant assay to measure LRRK2 pathway activity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our assay is a robust and reliable assay to quantify LKKR2 kinase pathway activity in human neutrophil lysates and is suitable for use in clinical trials and in the clinic.

LRRK2 phosphorylates Rab10 in human neutrophil lysates, and that this phosphorylation event is significantly higher in patients with the G2019S mutation in LRRK2 compared with sporadic PD and healthy control subjects.
the LRRK2 Rab10 kinase pathway assay described herein could provide a robust tool to assess the LRRK pathway in patients, and may find utility in clinical trials.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a novel and robust assay to measure LRRK2 Rab10 pathway activity in human neutrophil lysates.
our assay is robust, reproducible and can be easily adapted in a clinical setting.
our assay could be a useful tool for the assessment of LRRK kinase pathway activity and for patient stratification in clinical trials.
The main takeaway from our work is that
peripheral blood neutophils are a useful resource to assess LRRK2 pathway activity in Parkinson9s patients and healthy controls.
the LRRK2 Rab10 phosphorylation pathway is a promising biomarker of LRRK pathway activity and could be used to assess the pharmacodynamic effect of LRRK inhibitors in clinical trials.
